balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Midea Real Estate Holding Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

continuingRevenue.title: Reported vs continuing-operations revenue
continuingRevenue.content:
Reported revenue is the headline consolidated figure for the fiscal period as filed. Continuing-operations revenue restates each period as if the business distributed to shareholders had never been part of the group, so it is comparable across the spin-off.

For Midea Real Estate Holding Limited: in October 2024 the company distributed its entire heavy-asset property-development business in specie to shareholders, leaving a light-asset services platform (property management, asset operation, project management, real estate tech). Reported revenue fell from RMB73.6bn (FY2023) to RMB3.7bn (FY2024) -- a 95% drop that looks like a collapse but is the deliberate removal of the development business, not a decline in the ongoing company. Continuing-operations revenue is flat-to-growing across the same break (RMB2.8bn H1 FY2024-equivalent basis to RMB4.1bn FY2025).

What to watch:

  • Continuing-ops growth, not the reported-totals discontinuity
  • FY2023 and earlier reported bars are development-business-inclusive and not a like-for-like base

continuingIncome.title: Operating and net income: reported vs continuing
continuingIncome.content:
Operating income (continuing) and net income (continuing, attributable) are restated to exclude the distributed development business, isolating the profitability of the services platform that now constitutes the whole company.

For Midea Real Estate Holding Limited: reported net income went negative in FY2024 (-RMB2.06bn) almost entirely on one-off costs and losses recognised on the distribution itself. Continuing-operations net income attributable to owners was positive and growing through the same period: RMB375m (FY2023) to RMB478m (FY2024) to RMB559m (FY2025). The reported-income chart in Growth & Profitability above, read alone, would say the business lost money in FY2024; this chart is the correction.

What to watch:

  • Continuing operating income margin (now ~20%, far above the development business's historical single-digit margins)
  • Whether continuing net income keeps compounding now that the capital-intensive, low-margin development business is gone

continuingEps.title: EPS: reported vs continuing operations
continuingEps.content:
EPS (continuing ops) is earnings per share from the restated continuing business only, where disclosed.

For Midea Real Estate Holding Limited: reported EPS swung to -1.44 in FY2024 on the distribution-related charges; the company disclosed a positive continuing-ops EPS of 0.33 for the same year, which is the figure that reflects the ongoing services business shareholders actually hold today. Disclosure of this line is sparse (FY2024 only in the filings to date), so later periods show the gap rather than an implied zero.

What to watch:

  • Whether the company resumes disclosing EPSContinuing in later filings
  • Share count stability (1,430.6m, unchanged since the distribution) as the denominator

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Midea Real Estate Holding Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Midea Real Estate Holding Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Midea Real Estate Holding Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Midea Real Estate Holding Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Midea Real Estate Holding Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Midea Real Estate Holding Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Midea Real Estate Holding Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Midea Real Estate Holding Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
